title: Interference-induced dynamical crossovers in quantum walks on disordered square lattices
authors: Ramnarayan Bera, Arijit Roy, Soumyadip Ghosh, Soumen Roy
abstract: We study discrete-time quantum walks with Fourier, Grover, and Hadamard coin operators on disordered square lattices, alongside classical random walks. Edges in the lattice are absent with a probability, $p$. In this case, both classical and quantum walks exhibit an essentially identical degradation of transport. We then study a general version of this model, in which the existing edges are retained. However, the absent edges are no longer absent, but now become partially transmitting, with a transmission coefficient $f$. We find that the response is now quite sensitive to the walk protocol and coin symmetry. The classical walk exhibits asymptotic stability of the anomalous diffusion exponent, $β(t)$. In comparison, quantum walks exhibit a monotonically decaying $β(t)$ beyond the initial transient regime, leading to the absence of quantum diffusion in two dimensions. We map the transport regimes in the $(f,p)$ plane and identify the contour for $β=1$, which separates the subdiffusive and superdiffusive regimes. We also examine the effective diffusion coefficient, the inverse participation ratio, and the first two moments of edge transmission. We restrict ourselves to analyzing bulk propagation prior to finite-size boundary reflections. The results indicate that quantum transport depends significantly on coin-specific interference and cannot be fully described by transmission statistics alone.
summary: This paper investigates how quantum interference affects transport in disordered 2D lattices by comparing quantum walks to classical random walks. It finds that quantum transport decays dynamically towards localization, a behavior fundamentally different from classical diffusion. The work maps out the phase space governing these crossovers using various disorder parameters and coin symmetries.
main_problem: The study compares the transport dynamics of quantum walks versus classical random walks on disordered lattices to understand the role of quantum interference in transport resilience.
main_result: Quantum walks exhibit a monotonically decaying transport exponent, suggesting a tendency towards Anderson localization in 2D, unlike classical walks which maintain stable diffusion exponents.
method: The analysis uses time-dependent diagnostics like the transport exponent ($ eta(t)$) and Inverse Participation Ratio (IPR) to characterize spreading rates in the bulk propagation regime.
model_or_system: The system is a discrete-time quantum walk on a 2D square lattice, incorporating disorder via partially transmitting edges ($f$) with probability $p$. Three coin operators (Fourier, Grover, Hadamard) are tested.
key_observables: Transport exponent $ eta(t)$, Effective Diffusion Coefficient ($D_{eff}$), Inverse Participation Ratio (IPR), and the $ eta=1$ contour separating super- and subdiffusive regimes.
important_parameters: Disorder probability ($p$), transmission coefficient ($f$), and the specific coin operator used.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to bulk propagation before finite-size boundary reflections, and the observed $ eta=1$ contour is interpreted as a finite-time crossover, not a true phase transition.
figures_summary: Figures map the transport regimes ($ eta$ vs. $f, p$ plane) and show the temporal evolution of the local transport exponent $ eta_{	ext{local}}(t)$ for different disorder strengths.
paper_structure: The paper first compares quantum and classical transport on binary-percolated lattices, then generalizes to partially transmitting edges, analyzing the resulting transport regimes and highlighting the dependence on coin symmetry.
why_interesting: The clear distinction between quantum and classical transport scaling in the presence of disorder, particularly the evidence for localization driven by interference, is highly relevant to understanding wave propagation in disordered photonic or electronic structures.

The panels compare classical random walks (CRWs) with discrete-time quantum walks (DTQWs) using the Fourier (FC), Grover (GC), and Hadamard (HC) coin operators.

Panels (a)–(c) correspond to f = 0, (d)–(f) to f = 0.50, and (g)–(i) to f = 1.00 with defective edge probability written inside graphs. The curves compare quantum walks with Fourier (FC), Grover (GC), and Hadamard (HC) coins with the classical random walk (CRW).

FIG. 3: Transport-regime maps in the (f, p) plane. (a) Regions classified by the measured exponent: β < 1 indicates subdiffusive and β > 1 superdiffusive spreading. The contour β = 1 marks the crossover within the fitting window. (b) The corresponding β = 1 contours for the Fourier, Grover, and Hadamard coins.
